review_notes: I read the whole target file and the related files NativeCylinderLimit, NativeCylinderComparison, NativeCommRingCylinderSections and NativeAdditiveCylinderSections. I also looked at the named-preimage API in NativeOpenRestriction. I did not report the ring/additive `_eq` and `_restrict` wrappers: they are thin and cannot be factored further because they have different ambient categories. The `namedSectionRestriction_naturality` and `presheaf_cast_restrict` lemmas are already shared and reused. I did not compile the proposed changes, so the exact placement of the shared lemmas (NativeCylinderLimit versus a new upstream file) and the `rfl` claim are untested. I expect `rfl` to work because `stageMap` and `coneComponent` are plain `def`s whose bodies are exactly these `restrictOnNamedPreimage` terms. The import direction is fine: the target imports the ring and additive files, so a helper placed in NativeCylinderLimit (which those files already use) is visible to all of them.

findings.excerpt:
apply (cancel_mono ((S.obj (op i.1)).ofRestrict
    (stageOpen S i0 W i).isOpenEmbedding)).1
  exact (coneComponent_fac S i0 m W i).trans
findings.problem: The same `cancel_mono ofRestrict` plus `_fac.trans restrictOnNamedPreimage_fac.symm` argument is written out as `coneComponent_eq_named`, and again as `stageMap_eq_named` (lines 95-108). It also appears as the local `hcomponent` in three other files: NativeCylinderComparison, NativeCommRingCylinderSections and NativeAdditiveCylinderSections. That is at least five copies. In NativeCylinderLimit, `stageMap` and `coneComponent` are defined directly as `restrictOnNamedPreimage` with exactly the same arguments as the right-hand sides here. So the equations hold by `rfl`, and the monomorphism-cancellation proofs are re-proving a definitional unfolding.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the equation once, next to `coneComponent_fac` in NativeCylinderLimit, as a non-private lemma `coneComponent_eq_named` with the same statement. Its proof is `rfl`; if that fails, use the cancel_mono argument once. Do the same for `stageMap_eq_named`. Delete the private copies here (lines 95-108 and 226-239). Replace `hcomponent` in the other three files by the shared lemma. Alternatively, drop the lemmas and use `change`/`unfold coneComponent stageMap` at the use sites, as `stageMap_sections` already does via `change ... Γ.map (stageMap ...)`. At the use sites `rw [coneComponent_eq_named S i0 m W i]` and `rw [stageMap_eq_named S i0 W f.op]` stay unchanged and now point to the shared lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about 14 lines of Mono-cancellation boilerplate from each of five places. A change to the `ofRestrict` or `isOpenEmbedding` API then has one site to fix. Readers no longer wonder why a definitional equality needs a cancellation proof.

findings.excerpt:
rw [colimit_ι_cylinderSectionsComparison]
  change eqToHom (SheafedSpace.restrict_Γ_obj
      (S.obj (op i.1)) (stageOpen S i0 W i)).symm ≫
    SheafedSpace.Γ.map (coneComponent S i0 m W i).op ≫
findings.problem: This proof has the same mathematical content as `originalStage_nativeCommRingCylinderSectionsComparison`, `originalStage_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison` and `originalStage_restrictedGlobalSectionsComparison`. All four have the same statement shape. Each rewrites the coprojection with the comparison's defining `ι` law, then pushes `eqToHom ≫ Γ.map (coneComponent).op ≫ eqToHom` through `restrictOnNamedPreimage_Γ_map`. The only thing that differs is which map `φ` out of the colimit is used. The ring and additive versions even write out a long `calc` just to reassociate. The target then proves the generic comparison equal to the ring and additive ones (`ringCylinderSectionsComparison_eq`, `additiveCylinderSectionsComparison_eq`). This confirms that the four arguments are one argument.
findings.proposed_change: Add an upstream lemma, in NativeCylinderLimit or a small shared file. Statement: for any `φ : colimit ((restricted S i0 W).rightOp ⋙ SheafedSpace.Γ) ⟶ m.pt.presheaf.obj (op (coneOpen S i0 m W))` (under `[HasColimit _]`) with `hφ : colimit.ι _ i ≫ φ = SheafedSpace.Γ.map ((restrictedCone S i0 m W).π.app (op i)).op ≫ eqToHom (restrict_Γ_obj m.pt (coneOpen S i0 m W))`, we have `eqToHom (restrict_Γ_obj (S.obj (op i.1)) (stageOpen S i0 W i)).symm ≫ colimit.ι _ i ≫ φ = (m.π.app (op i.1)).hom.c.app (op (stageOpen S i0 W i)) ≫ eqToHom (congrArg ... (coneOpen_eq_stage S i0 m W i).symm)`. Proof: `rw [hφ]`, `change` to the `Γ.map (coneComponent ..).op` form, `rw [coneComponent_eq_named]`, and finish with `restrictOnNamedPreimage_Γ_map`. This is exactly lines 252-260. Then the generic theorem becomes the lemma applied with `colimit_ι_cylinderSectionsComparison`. The ring, additive and NativeCylinderComparison versions become the lemma applied with `colimit_ι_nativeCommRingCylinderSectionsComparison`, `colimit_ι_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison` and `colimit_ι_restrictedGlobalSectionsComparison`. Each of those is one line, and the three `calc` blocks disappear. `cylinderSections` is an abbrev for the same functor, so the statements match.
findings.benefit: The cone-component Γ-transport argument is stated and checked once instead of four times. It removes roughly 60 duplicated lines. It also makes explicit that the ring and additive comparisons satisfy the same arrow law as the generic one, and any later change to the named-preimage transports is made in one place.
